analysis.title: Copper - Oversold? ...Insurance premiums and Anglo cadence
key_insights: McGeoch argues for a cheap upside hedge in copper. Copper is about $12.5k versus $14.5k earlier, which he says removes a lot of risk premium.
Positioning cited as short across the board: CTAs short, China speculators short, macro funds short. CESCO and LME sentiment is described as bearish with no stated reason.
He expects US downstream development to depend on upstream metal availability, and says the arbitrage points to US exports. Rare earths and the US/China relationship are named as the main complexity.

Copper miners are described as oversold. The GSXGCOPP basket is at an 8-month low, the tail of smaller COPX names has been removed, balance sheets sit at 0.0-0.5x net debt/EBITDA, seasonality is a tailwind, and the P/B long/short ratio is at a 6-month low.

The case rests on a stockout being priced. Prior examples cited: gas in 2022, cocoa in 2024, alumina in 2023, bauxite in 2025, lumber during covid, and steel rallying 5x after covid. He notes alumina and bauxite were bearish and were not supply constrained as copper is.
Three triggers would pay the trade: demand improves, supply disappoints, or tariffs come in. He says a tariff would send the copper price back up quickly.

Single-stock idea: the market keeps returning to Anglo American (AAL.LN). A news item says remedy discussions are nearing conclusion and no structural remedies are being discussed, according to a third source.
Anglo deal sequence the market is following: diamonds deal completion, nickel (EU ruling date Dec 21, about $500m), the Teck deal approval described as the main event, then the coal deal.
After the Teck deal closes, a dividend is due 45 days post close, and an index event follows with feedback of more than $5bn of passive demand.
The coal deal needs FIRB approval (1Q target), with $2.3bn upfront and a $1.575m earn-out over 5 years. The author asks whether a buyback follows.
Glencore buyback read-through: about 58% of the $500m programme has been bought, as an indicator of how miners with buybacks view their shares at current levels.

market_movers.rationale: Anglo American is the single-stock way to express the view. The market is tracking a deal cadence of diamonds, nickel, Teck approval, then the coal deal, with remedy talks reported as nearing conclusion.
Glencore has bought about 58% of its $500m buyback as the stock moved lower.

sector_views.rationale: Miners are oversold with the basket at an 8-month low, low leverage (0.0-0.5x ND/EBITDA), a seasonal tailwind and a P/B long/short ratio at a 6-month low. The author frames upside optionality as cheap insurance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from $14.5k, which the author reads as a large amount of risk premium removed.

trade_ideas.description: Buy GSXGCOPP (copper miners basket) March 130%/140% call spread for 1% premium, 10x payout
trade_ideas.rationale: Pays if demand improves, supply disappoints or tariffs come in. All three are priced in the basket, which is at an 8-month low, with low leverage and seasonal support.
trade_ideas.risk: Maximum loss is the premium paid.

trade_ideas.description: Long Anglo American (AAL.LN) as the single-stock copper expression
trade_ideas.rationale: The market follows a deal cadence: diamonds, nickel, Teck approval with a dividend and passive index demand over $5bn, then the coal deal.

risk_factors: Copper may keep falling if tariffs do not come in and demand does not improve.
Alumina and bauxite stockout pricing ended up bearish, so the direction of a stockout move is uncertain.
Anglo American deal approvals (EU nickel ruling Dec 21, FIRB for coal) could slip.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs, China speculators and macro funds are short copper.
P/B long/short ratio for the copper miners basket is at a 6-month low.
GSXGCOPP Mar 130%/140% call spread costs 1% for a 10x payout, with maximum loss limited to the premium paid.
geopolitical: US/China relationship and rare earths cited as the main complexity for metals.
Possible US tariff on copper, which the author says would send the price back up quickly.
EU ruling on the Anglo American nickel deal expected Dec 21.

tension_points.bull_case: Copper fell from $14.5k to $12.5k with CTAs, China speculators and macro funds short. A demand recovery, a supply disappointment or a tariff would each pay a cheap call spread, and the miners basket is at an 8-month low with low leverage.
tension_points.bear_case: Past stockout pricing in alumina and bauxite was bearish, and the author says the market does not know whether a stockout is bearish or bullish. Sentiment at CESCO and LME is bearish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US tariff not being imposed, which the author says is the main condition for the price to rocket back.
